name: gpp
why: A general-purpose preprocessor with user-definable syntax, a strange tool for rewriting text in arbitrary grammars.

brief.what_it_is: GPP is a general-purpose preprocessor, a command-line tool that rewrites text by expanding macros. Its syntax is customizable, so it is not tied to one programming language. It has built-in macro sets for C/C++, LaTeX, HTML, XHTML, and Prolog files. It takes an input file containing text and macro calls, and writes the expanded text out. The README also says the project's own documentation is generated by GPP from a macro file (gpp.pp) in HTML, LaTeX, or troff (man page) output.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage presents GPP as a middle path between the C preprocessor, which is much more tied to C-family languages, and GNU m4, whose syntax the author describes as heavier and less flexible than GPP's.
brief.how_it_works: The README says GPP's syntax can be customized, which is what lets one tool serve many languages. It ships built-in macros for several formats. The READMEs do not describe the internal mechanism in more detail.

commands_seen.context: Source install from the portable tarball; the README says this should work in most cases if make and a C compiler are present.
After installing, runs GPP on its own documentation source to generate the HTML docs; the README says this is also a basic functionality test.

brief.install_notes: Source tarballs (.tar.bz2) come from GitHub releases or nothingisreal.com, and the included INSTALL file has the steps. Needs make and a C compiler. Windows is not covered by the standard steps: the README suggests Cygwin or MSYS, or else hand-editing config.h.in into src/config.h and compiling src/gpp.c with HAVE_CONFIG_H defined (and WIN_NT if the compiler does not define it). Building from the GitHub development version requires setting up GNU Autotools by hand. Binary packages exist for Debian, FreeBSD, macOS, openSUSE, Ubuntu and Fedora, but they are made by third parties, and the authors take no responsibility for them.
brief.standout: GPP lets you define the macro syntax itself, so one tool can handle C, LaTeX, HTML, Prolog, or anything else, where cpp is tied to C and m4 has a fixed, heavier syntax. Its own documentation is produced by running GPP on a macro file, which the README calls instructive.
brief.status: Maintained, with evidence from the homepage: latest stable version 2.28, released 2023-09-26, and the maintainer is Tristan Miller, who has maintained it since version 2.12. I did not see commit dates or a recent-activity signal in the pages I read, so the current pace is not confirmed.
brief.caveats: Free software under the GNU Lesser General Public Licence. Windows support needs Cygwin, MSYS, or manual config editing. Third-party binary packages are not vouched for by the authors. The development version needs Autotools set up by hand.
quotes: GPP is a general-purpose preprocessor with customizable syntax, suitable for a wide range of preprocessing tasks.
Its independence from any one programming language makes it much more versatile than the C preprocessor (cpp), while its syntax is lighter and more flexible than that of GNU m4.
Studying this file should prove instructive, and manually running it through GPP can serve as a basic test of the program's functionality.
